notes: Object insert through has_species, the inverse of in_genus. "The genus Sphenodon belongs to the order Rhynchocephalia" is the class axiom that the genus's species are rhynchocephalians. The edit's "living" is a class. Every entity is distinct: the record calls the species newly described and different from the tuatara. The 'only' question (q2) is determinate no: adding the closed fact to the KB is inconsistent with the new, distinct living species. The two worlds differ only on the count (fol), so they carry no axioms. (2026-10-31: q2 was indeterminate with w1 keeping the closed fact as an exception world; the record now makes it determinate, FINDINGS A1.)

queries.not_checked: fol (arithmetic): counts the members of a group

fol.notes: Species are an uninterpreted sort (the tuatara, Sphenodon kerewai); being in the genus Sphenodon, a rhynchocephalian and living are beliefs (uninterpreted predicates). The genus-to-order fact is the DL file's sphenodon_order. With one known member no distinctness presupposition is needed among the old ones. w1 stores the count as a figure (number_of_members, ATTRIBUTES.md), which the insert does not recompute; w2 stores the counting rule over the stored list (each named member counted once: an entry counts only if it differs from the earlier ones, so the distinctness presupposition enters the count). Counting needs a closed world: the known members are distinct and every member the model knows is one of the named constants (presuppositions; named_only is what the counting rule rests on, though Z3 does not need it to fix the value). The new member's distinctness from the named ones is part of the edit ('newly described/discovered').

sphenodon_order.says: The genus Sphenodon (the tuatara) belongs to the reptile order Rhynchocephalia: its species are rhynchocephalians.

tuatara.says: The tuatara is a living species of the genus Sphenodon. (stored)

named_only.says: Every living rhynchocephalian the model knows of is one of the named species. (closed world)
named_only.z3: ForAll(s, Implies(And(living(s), rhynchocephalian(s)), Or(s == tuatara, s == kerewai)))

stores: number_of_members(rhynchocephalians) == count(And(living(tuatara), rhynchocephalian(tuatara)), And(And(living(kerewai), rhynchocephalian(kerewai)), tuatara != kerewai))
